interlude_1.speaker: dad
interlude_1.text: There. Page one's dry. Wrinkled, but the meadow pops up again. Mostly.

interlude_1.speaker: nell
interlude_1.text: The fox's tail is gone. Half the pages are stuck together. It's ruined, Dad.

interlude_1.speaker: gran
interlude_1.text: Ruined is when you stop fixing it, love. Your grandad's mug has three glue lines and I'd fight anyone who tried to bin it.

interlude_1.speaker: nell
interlude_1.text: It's not the same, though. Nothing's the same. The house isn't even ours anymore.

interlude_1.speaker: dad
interlude_1.text: I'll do the next page tomorrow, all the same. You can help, if you want. Or just sit there and be angry. Both count.

interlude_2.speaker: dad
interlude_2.text: Harbor page. The lanterns came up better than I thought. The boat's held together with about a metre of tape, but it floats. Well. It would.

interlude_2.speaker: dad
interlude_2.text: There's a bit under the flap I can't get dry. The ink keeps running, no matter what I...

interlude_2.speaker: nell
interlude_2.text: Just stop. It's never going to be the same. None of it. You can tape it and iron it all night and it's still going to be wrecked.

interlude_2.speaker: nell
interlude_2.text: No. I'm going to bed. Don't wait up for the book. It's not coming back.

interlude_3.speaker: narrator
interlude_3.text: Dad had fallen asleep at the table. The lamp was still on. The book lay open at the winter page, its spine split down the middle.

interlude_3.speaker: gran
interlude_3.text: Let him sleep, love. He's been up every night since we got here.

interlude_3.speaker: nell
interlude_3.text: It's worse. Look. The middle's coming apart. The fox is just... gone. The page he was on is empty.

interlude_3.speaker: gran
interlude_3.text: Mm. It'll need more than one pair of hands, that bit.

interlude_3.speaker: nell
interlude_3.text: He kept the torn bit. The fox's tail. It's in an envelope. He wrote 'Patch, tail' on it.

interlude_3.speaker: gran
interlude_3.text: Your dad doesn't throw out the bits that come off. Never has.

interlude_3.speaker: narrator
interlude_3.text: Nell looked at the hairdryer at the end of the table for a long time. She didn't pick it up. Not yet.

interlude_3.speaker: narrator
interlude_3.text: Down in the middle of the book, in the dark, something small was still moving.
